name: Vesica Piscis & Mandorla — Geometry, Centers, Axis and Door
purpose: Provide the canonical mathematical geometry for Vesica Piscis/Mandorla and explicitly distinguish circle centers, relational/lens center, symmetry axes and Potatoverse mappings. Mathematical facts are separated from historical symbolism and project interpretation.
epistemic_rule: Geometry is mathematical. Art-history claims require historical sources. Potatoverse mappings—Father/Sun circle, Earth/humanity circle, Son/Door overlap, Tim as source-center or Axis reference—are project interpretations and do not follow from the geometry itself.

vesica_piscis.definition: The Vesica Piscis is the lens-shaped intersection of two congruent circles whose center separation equals their common radius r.

key_geometry.correction: The archive's previous value approximately 0.6141848493 r² was half of the full lens area and has been corrected.

vesica_piscis.derivation: The full lens consists of two congruent circular segments. Equivalently A=2[(πr²/3)-(√3 r²/4)]=(2π/3-√3/2)r²=(1/6)(4π-3√3)r².
vesica_piscis.angles: The radii from either circle center to the two intersection points subtend 120 degrees for the intersecting segment geometry; the center-to-center/intersection triangles are equilateral with 60 degree angles. Care is needed not to confuse the equilateral-triangle 60-degree angles with the full sector used in the lens-area calculation.
vesica_piscis.symmetry: The line joining C1 and C2 is the horizontal symmetry axis. The perpendicular bisector x=0 through P± is the vertical symmetry axis. Their intersection CR is the geometric center of the lens relation.

center_taxonomy.C1_C2: centers intrinsic to each complete parent circle; each can represent its own domain/source/reference
center_taxonomy.CR: midpoint created by relation between the two parent centers and center of the overlap lens; belongs naturally to the relationship rather than exclusively to either circle
center_taxonomy.intersection_points: threshold points where both circle boundaries simultaneously meet
center_taxonomy.axis_crossing: CR is also where horizontal and vertical symmetry axes cross
center_taxonomy.project_warning: Calling Tim 'the center' is incomplete unless the archive states whether Tim means source-circle center, relational lens center, Axis/reference center or another center type.

mandorla.definition: Mandorla ('almond') is the art-historical term for an almond/lens-shaped sacred enclosure or aureole. Some mandorlae use Vesica-like geometry, but not every mandorla is mathematically a standard Vesica Piscis.
mandorla.historical_use: Especially prominent in Byzantine and medieval Christian art around Christ, the Virgin and other sacred figures, often marking divine glory, manifestation or a threshold between ordinary and transcendent space.
mandorla.potatoverse_value: The mandorla supplies an especially good visual Door/Vessel because it is not either parent circle but the shared region in which two complete domains are simultaneously present.

recommended_default.source_center: Tim/Father as source-center of upper/source domain
recommended_default.relational_center: center of Door/overlap; not automatically identical with Father/source-center
recommended_default.vertical_axis: Ladder/Axis connecting upper and lower readings through the overlap

potatoverse_mapping.why_this_mapping_is_stronger: It preserves the mature identity-to-infrastructure law: Father is source/orientation/House; Son is interface/Door; their relation creates a shared region without erasing either domain. It also allows Tim to be 'center' in a source/orientational sense without forcing Tim to occupy the Son's Door-center geometrically.
potatoverse_mapping.stereo_theoism: The two complete circles can still support the project's Stereo Theoism/non-dual-dualism: two differentiated lenses/domains create a third shared region. The overlap is relation, not annihilation of difference.
potatoverse_mapping.eye_relation: The pointed lens resembles an Eye/almond/doorway in project symbolism; mathematically this resemblance has no theological content until mapped.
potatoverse_mapping.birth_canal_relation: The lens can function as project birth-canal/threshold imagery because it is a bounded passage between differentiated fields; this remains interpretive symbolism.

sun_moon_earth_extension.principle: Do not force Sun, Moon and Earth into a literal two-circle astronomy diagram. Instead use Vesica as relational topology: Source/illumination field and embodied/observer field overlap through Door, while Moon can occupy a reflector/mediator role inside or adjacent to the embodied side depending the diagram.
sun_moon_earth_extension.moon: reflected/phase-dependent mediator rather than independent source
sun_moon_earth_extension.door: shared relation in which source becomes perceivable/actionable to embodied observer

mesopotamian_geometry_neighbor.finding: MathWorld's reconstruction of the Old Babylonian 'ox-eye' or Babylonian bull's-eye identifies a figure geometrically equivalent to a Vesica Piscis.
mesopotamian_geometry_neighbor.importance: This creates a historically interesting Mesopotamia↔Eye↔Vesica mathematical neighbor for the archive.
mesopotamian_geometry_neighbor.boundary: It does not demonstrate an ancient Babylonian doctrine of Christ, Door, Tim, Potato of Life or the project's metaphysics.

mathematical_notes: Scaling by k multiplies all lengths by k and area by k² while preserving shape.
The figure has two reflection axes and 180-degree rotational symmetry.
Each parent circle remains complete; overlap does not subtract the identity of either parent domain.
CR is midpoint/balance of the two circle centers, not the center of either parent circle.
The two intersection points are equal-distance from C1 and C2, making them natural mathematical boundary-agreement points.
research_questions: Recover the exact Potatoverse diagram that assigned Tim, Son, Jesus, Earth and Heaven to upper/lower circles and lens.
Audit every repository use of 'center' and tag it as source-center, lens-center, symmetry-center, dynamical/barycentric center, orientational center or attention-center.
Study historically sourced mandorla examples before making stronger Christian iconographic claims.
Compare the Babylonian ox-eye construction with actual tablet scholarship rather than using MathWorld alone for historical interpretation.
Keep any 3D extension explicitly separate from the canonical 2D geometry.
